name: LSND
summary: LSND operated at LAMPF/LANSCE, Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico. Its dark-matter role in this record primarily comes from later theoretical reinterpretations of a historical neutrino experiment.
detection_principle: Data from the original neutrino detector test electron scattering of beam-associated dark matter and visible light-scalar decays; acceptance and backgrounds must be recalculated for new production and detection models.

results.summary: Studies of historical LSND samples constrain part of MeV-dark-matter parameter space, without new data-taking.
Historical data were further used to constrain light Higgs-portal scalars.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered. This record includes reinterpretations of historical data in new models. A reinterpretation paper's publication year is not the apparatus operating year, and the original experiment may primarily have targeted neutrinos, axions or other light particles.
